projects.name: Cross-Carrier Wave
projects.I: Provenance-preserving carrier/transform experiments across representations and domains.
projects.R: Faithful compression/translation/abstraction must remain distinct from concealed consequential loss.
projects.P: Use adaptive typed carriers, explicit transform states, one-degree probes, and carried loss/remainder.
projects.O: Adaptive carrier overlays and explicit loss accounting were retained; universal-theory interpretations were rejected.
projects.highlight: Transform contracts now carry provenance, change, loss, uncertainty, ethics/cost, and remainder.
projects.lowlight: Early fixed-dimensional and universal-coordinate readings exceeded the evidence.
projects.claimCeiling: Research architecture; not a completed theory of knowledge or universal semantic geometry.

checks.assumption: Consequential distinctions can be identified locally enough to test preservation.
checks.test: Ablate or alter one carrier/transform relation and test reconstructibility.
checks.unknown: Broad real-world benefit outside bounded experiments remains unestablished.

projects.name: Orbit Library
projects.I: A compact active navigation surface with recoverable source/history/support layers.
projects.R: Useful navigation is not exhaustive historical identity or evidence authority.
projects.P: Prefer source-native reconstruction, exact identity, cold locators when earned, and explicit unknown/unassigned states.
projects.O: Compact navigation works, but root-edge audits proved exact file-level historical coverage remains partial.
projects.highlight: Current/history/support and exact-source boundaries became explicit.
projects.lowlight: Later historical catalogs omitted genuine predecessor identities.
projects.claimCeiling: Navigation/recovery infrastructure; not a complete model of the Library.

checks.assumption: A small active surface is preferable when exact recovery remains possible.
checks.test: Freeze loose-root samples and measure exact recovery, family representation, ambiguity, and unresolved cases.
checks.unknown: The benefit/cost threshold for broader exact-file indexing remains unresolved.

projects.name: Tiny Babel / TBCL
projects.I: Finite language/retrieval/reorganization research plus later TBCL runtime/reconstruction work.
projects.R: Subject/obligation must remain distinct from carrier/index/hierarchy/runtime representation.
projects.P: Preserve the finite subject, exact verification boundary, strict semantics, and source/reconstruction separation.
projects.O: Finite exhaustive verification and carrier reduction succeeded within bounded inherited domains.
projects.highlight: Exhaustive finite verification replaced example-only confidence.
projects.lowlight: Finite success does not imply universal language, retrieval, or global minimality.

checks.assumption: The finite subject/query space faithfully represents the bounded claim.
checks.test: Exhaustive enumeration plus behavior comparison across carriers and independent verification where possible.
checks.unknown: Scaling to open-ended/noisy/culturally variable domains remains unresolved.

projects.name: Operator Moonshot
projects.I: Bounded mathematical, computational, educational, operator, and calibration experiments.
projects.R: Interesting mechanism, replicated result, general scientific claim, and open-problem solution are different evidence levels.
projects.P: Replicate before promotion, preserve failed replications, use calibration only as calibration, and attack with counterexamples/ablations.
projects.O: Evidence discipline strengthened; Cycle 3 replication and Education E3 robustness failures remain preserved.
projects.highlight: Causal ablation, replication, provenance, and claim ceilings became core practice.
projects.lowlight: Several promising branches failed replication/robustness and some original source remains missing.
projects.claimCeiling: Research laboratory/evidence ledger; not proof that larger open targets are solved.

checks.assumption: The experiment target, baseline, and evidence carrier actually measure the claimed relation.
checks.test: Replication, ablation, adversarial counterexamples, independent verification, and simpler baselines.
checks.unknown: Generalization outside finite/synthetic domains remains unresolved.

projects.name: Model Experiments
projects.I: PulseNet, PulseNet GP, SPDM, streaming/recurrent memory, Micro-Ouro, compressed-domain and related model experiments.
projects.R: Mechanism activity, usefulness, and causality must be tested separately.
projects.P: Keep runnable baselines, ablate proposed mechanisms, compare against trivial alternatives, and preserve regressions.
projects.O: Reusable machinery and negative evidence accumulated; several mechanisms changed outputs without earning usefulness claims.
projects.highlight: Model work increasingly separated execution correctness, numerical stability, and predictive usefulness.
projects.lowlight: Regressions, baseline errors, weak reasoning cores, and below-chance checkpoints were found and retained.
projects.claimCeiling: Bounded implementation/experiment evidence; no general intelligence or universal reasoning claim.

checks.assumption: Benchmarks distinguish proposed mechanisms from simpler alternatives.
checks.test: Frozen data/baselines, ablation, multi-seed reruns, held-out performance, and stability checks.
checks.unknown: Value after training, scaling, native implementation, domain shift, and stronger baselines remains unresolved.

projects.name: Geometry, 4D Codecs, and Observer Experiments
projects.I: 3D/4D geometry, topology, inversion, compact encodings, finite observer/classification, and float64 carrier experiments.
projects.R: Useful/correct representation is not evidence of physical truth.
projects.P: Test round trips, corruption, inverse transforms, finite confounds, and raw-bit/numeric boundaries independently.
projects.O: Engineering mechanisms survived; over-strong physical interpretations and rigid fixed-dimensional stories were rejected.
projects.highlight: Encoding correctness and observer distinguishability became independently testable.
projects.lowlight: Geometric resemblance and finite discrimination can invite interpretations beyond the evidence.
projects.claimCeiling: Engineering and bounded mathematical experiments; no new physical theory claim.

checks.assumption: Encoding/transform specifications are explicit enough for independent testing.
checks.test: Exact encode/decode, perturbation, inverse-transform, confound enumeration, ablation, and integrity checks.
checks.unknown: Which representations correspond to deeper physical structure, if any, remains unresolved.

projects.name: Historical Recovery
projects.I: Old code, generic pasted sources, archives, later summaries, incomplete indexes, and source-native recovery evidence.
projects.R: Not found by an index is not absence; semantic resemblance is not project identity.
projects.P: Follow exact file IDs, chronology, archive membership, namespaces, migrations, and source hashes before assigning identity.
projects.O: Hidden predecessor identities were recovered; Fuzzball remains an explicit unresolved carrier and a prior black-hole conflation was corrected.
projects.highlight: FractalDeflectiveEngine and GrandUnifiedPerceptron predecessor identities were recovered from obscured carriers.
projects.lowlight: Fuzzball and the original structured solver/operator-lab source remain unresolved gaps; some archive bytes are inaccessible.
projects.claimCeiling: Recovery graph only; missing carriers remain unresolved rather than substituted.

checks.assumption: User-attested historical projects are legitimate recovery targets without implying a relation to candidate files.
checks.test: Exact source, namespace, archive path, hash, chronology, and independent migration/provenance references.
checks.unknown: The exact Fuzzball carrier, chronology, and relation to neighboring projects remain unresolved.
